title: How configuration is resolved
caption: Three ways a config can arrive, one load per session, and a loud failure for anything the native boundary does not support.

nodes.flag: Passing --config or -c points at an exact JSON or JSONC file. Nothing else is searched.
nodes.discovery: Without a flag, the tool searches upward from the working directory for one .oxlintrc.json/.oxlintrc.jsonc or .oxfmtrc.json/.oxfmtrc.jsonc.
nodes.viteplus: Through the npm companions, a Vite+ vite.config.* can supply lint and fmt options, materialized through canonical OXC's public extends model.
nodes.session: The winning config is loaded and compiled exactly once when the native session starts. There is no per-file rediscovery.
nodes.overrides: overrides blocks and ignorePatterns are resolved against your authored paths, so **/*.tsrx patterns keep working.
nodes.batch: Every file in the batch reuses the same compiled session. Ordinary JS and TS files take the direct canonical path with the same options.
nodes.loud: An unsupported field fails the command before any parse or write. Nothing is silently ignored, so your config never lies to you.

steps.label: Choose a source
steps.caption: An explicit flag wins, upward discovery is the default, and Vite+ can forward options through the npm companions.

steps.label: Load once
steps.caption: One load, one compile, at session start. The benchmark gates pin this: one config load per session, no matter how many files.

steps.label: Apply per file
steps.caption: Overrides and ignore patterns match your authored paths while the whole batch shares the compiled session.

steps.label: Fail loudly
steps.caption: Anything unsupported stops the command with a clear error instead of quietly changing behavior.
